text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Macedonian government proposes restrictive changes in the law on pensions and social security. The government expects profit of some 80 million denars (some three million German marks).

- Macedonia and Bulgaria connected by fibre-optical cables as part of TransBalkan telecommunications system. Opening cerenomies in Kriva Palanka (Macedonia) and Kjustendil (Bulgaria) attended by Macedonian transport and communications minister Dimitar Buzlevski and President of Bulgarian telecommunications committee Ljubomir Kolarov.
- "The illegal Tetovo University" was one of the main topics at the closed round table talks between representatives of the OSCE, ethnic Albanians and the Macedonian government.
- French defence minister Charles Millon to visit Macedonia on Sunday. French-Macedonian agreement on military cooperation to be signed.

- The association of Macedonian judges rejects opposition parties accusations they are protecting the government and the ruling SDAM party. Macedonian judges are not to blame for problems with electoral lists in Macedonia.
- The association of independent trade unions to organize protest outside the government demanding better conditions for workers and payment of several months overdue salaries.
- The trade union of taxi and truck drivers to organize blockade of streets in front of the government for two hours.
- Miners from the Sasa mine in Makedonska Kamenica on strike over late salaries. The mine's management says there is no money to pay workers. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201196
